text.p: Any eventual deal between Portuguese building companies Engil-SGPS and Edifer is likely to fall short of an outright merger of the two companies, analysts said.
Giving a first quick reaction to Wednesday's news of talks between the two concerns, analysts said that a future partnership could involve a share exchange and cooperation in specific projects.
Engil, whose shares were gaining sharply on the Lisbon bourse, announced that it was in talks with Edifer on "harmonising" and "integrating" business strategies.
It gave no further details and said the degree of the proposed integration would be decided during the course of the talks.
Its stock was up nine percent at 2,375 escudos having touched a high of 2,400 escudos.
"I do not believe in a fusion of the two companies or in the purchase of (Edifer) by the other," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
"I think that the most probable scenario will be an exchange of shares and the development of some business together," said another analyst.
A source close to Edifer said in terms of activity inside Portugal, the company ranked fifth in turnover. Engil is fourth.

Edifer, which is owned by the Pires Coelho family, had turnover of 41 billion escudos in 1996. Engil had turnover of 62 billion escudos last year when it posted a profit of 1.5 billion escudos, up from 1.2 billion the previous year.
